mechanism_narrative: A sustained federal funds rate below 2.5% compresses discount rates for equity cash flows, generating positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as corporate financing costs decline.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when FEDFUNDS remains below 2.5%.

mechanism_narrative: Unemployment rate exceeding 4.0% in a 3-month window signals labor market deterioration that reduces consumer spending and corporate earnings growth, causing negative S&P 500 returns over 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 45% of instances when UNRATE exceeds 4.0%.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous decline in FEDFUNDS and rise in CPIAUCSL indicates central bank's aggressive inflation response, driving positive equity returns as market prices soft landing over 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint FEDFUNDS decline/CPIAUCSL rise fails to produce positive 60-day returns in more than 55% of cases, or Rank IC < 0.02.

mechanism_narrative: High inflation regimes (CPIAUCSL > 3.0% YoY) trigger market anticipation of aggressive rate hikes, compressing equity valuations and generating negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 45% of periods when CPIAUCSL exceeds 3.0%.

mechanism_narrative: Rising industrial production (INDPRO > 105) signals robust manufacturing output that supports corporate earnings growth, driving positive S&P 500 returns over 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when INDPRO exceeds 105.

mechanism_narrative: Housing starts below 1.2 million units annually indicate weakening real estate demand, reducing consumer wealth and spending, causing negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 45% of instances when HOUST is below 1.2 million.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous decline in PAYEMS and rise in UNRATE signals labor market weakening that reduces consumer confidence and corporate revenue growth, generating negative S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: The joint PAYEMS decline/UNRATE rise fails to produce negative 60-day returns in more than 55% of cases, or Rank IC > -0.02.

mechanism_narrative: Manufacturing contraction (INDPRO < 100) signals economic slowdown that reduces corporate earnings, causing negative S&P 500 returns over 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 45% of periods when INDPRO is below 100.
